packet.headline_seed: Watch Texas police officer pull man from burning car
packet.description_seed: Bodycam and dashcam footage shows a police officer rescue a man seconds before his car was engulfed in flames in Texas.

what: Watch Texas police officer pull man from burning car

clean_source_blocks.text: by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk SOUTHLAKE, Texas (TNND) — A Texas police officer is being recognized for a dramatic rescue after pulling a driver from a burning car just moments before the vehicle became engulfed in flames. Dashcam and body camera footage released by the Southlake Police Department shows Cpl. Joshua Swisher sprinting toward a smoke-filled Nissan Altima on June 7 while conducting an unrelated traffic stop along westbound Highway 114 in Southlake, Texas. Police said Swisher was alerted over his radio to a vehicle pouring heavy smoke as it approached his location. He directed the driver to pull onto the shoulder, but flames quickly intensified after the car came to a stop.

Body camera video shows Swisher repeatedly yelling, "Get out! Get out!" before rushing to the driver's door. When the exterior door handle snapped off in his hand, preventing him from opening it, he grabbed a window-breaking tool, shattered the driver's side window and pulled the trapped motorist to safety. Seconds later, the vehicle was fully engulfed in flames. "I could not even see inside the vehicle," Swisher told KDFW. "The only thing I saw was hands, and it was the driver trying to get his door open from the inside." The driver was not seriously injured, according to police. Swisher suffered only minor burns to his arm during the rescue. The Southlake Police Department later presented Swisher with its Meritorious Conduct Award, the department's second-highest honor.

The smoking vehicle had passed by Swisher on the highway, according to dashcam footage shared by the Southlake Police Department in a Facebook post. Swisher began following the vehicle in his car and had just directed it to the shoulder when it suddenly burst into flames. The dashcam and Swisher's body camera both captured the moment the burning car door handle broke off when he tried to open it. "Now, I'm thinking, 'How am I gonna get him out of this car?' And from there, I just put my gloves on," Swisher said. The camera footage shows thick, black smoke billowing from the car's windows with the driver still trapped inside. "I couldn't see inside the vehicle because of the amount of smoke that was pouring out," Swisher recalled.

Cpl. Joshua Swisher says he was at the "right place in the right time." A Texas police officer is speaking out after rescuing a driver from a burning car last month. Southlake Police Department Cpl. Joshua Swisher said he was responding to a traffic stop on June 7, along State Highway 114, when he received a call about a vehicle with heavy smoke pouring from it. "I had a vehicle pulled over on the shoulder, and almost simultaneously, dispatch alerted me to a smoke investigation, possible vehicle fire," Swisher told ABC News. "I was just thinking, 'I gotta get to that vehicle, get it stopped and pulled over, and see if I can't get that driver out of the vehicle before it goes up in flames.'"

by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk

SOUTHLAKE, Texas (TNND)  — A Texas police officer is being recognized for a dramatic rescue after pulling a driver from a burning car just moments before the vehicle became engulfed in flames.

Dashcam and body camera footage released by the Southlake Police Department shows Cpl. Joshua Swisher sprinting toward a smoke-filled Nissan Altima on June 7 while conducting an unrelated traffic stop along westbound Highway 114 in Southlake, Texas.

Police said Swisher was alerted over his radio to a vehicle pouring heavy smoke as it approached his location. He directed the driver to pull onto the shoulder, but flames quickly intensified after the car came to a stop.

Body camera video shows Swisher repeatedly yelling, "Get out! Get out!" before rushing to the driver's door. When the exterior door handle snapped off in his hand, preventing him from opening it, he grabbed a window-breaking tool, shattered the driver's side window and pulled the trapped motorist to safety. Seconds later, the vehicle was fully engulfed in flames.

"I could not even see inside the vehicle," Swisher told KDFW. "The only thing I saw was hands, and it was the driver trying to get his door open from the inside."

The driver was not seriously injured, according to police. Swisher suffered only minor burns to his arm during the rescue.

The Southlake Police Department later presented Swisher with its Meritorious Conduct Award, the department's second-highest honor.

"Corporal Swisher's courage, decisive action, and commitment to protecting others exemplify the highest standards of our profession," Southlake Police Capt. Blas Hernandez said in announcing the award. Police Chief Ashleigh Casey added that the rescue reflects "the commitment and character our officers bring to this job every day."

Swisher, however, downplayed his actions, saying any officer in the department would have responded the same way.

"I think I speak for every Southlake officer when I say that if anybody had been put in that same situation, same circumstances, any other officer would have done the same thing," he said. "That's what we want to do — save lives."

The rescue has since gone viral after the department released the dramatic dashcam and body camera footage showing how quickly the fire spread and how narrowly the driver escaped.

[Lähde: ABC7 News | URL: https://abc7news.com/story/officer-speaks-rescuing-driver-trapped-burning-car/19545038/]
Cpl. Joshua Swisher says he was at the "right place in the right time."

A Texas police officer is speaking out after rescuing a driver from a burning car last month.

Southlake Police Department Cpl. Joshua Swisher said he was responding to a traffic stop on June 7, along State Highway 114, when he received a call about a vehicle with heavy smoke pouring from it.

"I had a vehicle pulled over on the shoulder, and almost simultaneously, dispatch alerted me to a smoke investigation, possible vehicle fire," Swisher told ABC News. "I was just thinking, 'I gotta get to that vehicle, get it stopped and pulled over, and see if I can't get that driver out of the vehicle before it goes up in flames.'"

The smoking vehicle had passed by Swisher on the highway, according to dashcam footage shared by the Southlake Police Department in a Facebook post. Swisher began following the vehicle in his car and had just directed it to the shoulder when it suddenly burst into flames.

The dashcam and Swisher's body camera both captured the moment the burning car door handle broke off when he tried to open it.

"Now, I'm thinking, 'How am I gonna get him out of this car?' And from there, I just put my gloves on," Swisher said.

The camera footage shows thick, black smoke billowing from the car's windows with the driver still trapped inside.

"I couldn't see inside the vehicle because of the amount of smoke that was pouring out," Swisher recalled.

Because he couldn't open the car door, Swisher said he decided to break the car window with his fist in order to pull the driver out to safety.

"When the window shattered, that was a little bit of relief for me. 'Cause I knew I had an exit point at that time," he said.

Camera footage shows Swisher dragging the driver from the car as it becomes engulfed in flames, pulling him to safety.

According to Swisher, the driver, who was the only person in the car, was shaken, but able to walk away without serious injuries.

"It's not every day that something like this happens but I was just glad to be in the right place in the right time," Swisher said.

The Southlake Police Department honored Swisher with its second-highest honor, the Meritorious Conduct Award, for his quick-thinking and lifesaving actions that day. The award recognizes police employees who demonstrate exceptional courage, professionalism and performance while facing significant danger, according to the department.

payload.title: Poliisi pelasti kuljettajan palavasta autosta Texasissa – ovenkahva irtosi kesken pelastusyrityksen
payload.summary: Poliisi Joshua Swisher rikkoi savun täyttämän auton ikkunan ja veti kuljettajan turvaan vain sekunteja ennen kuin ajoneuvo oli kokonaan liekeissä.
payload.content:
Texasin Southlakessa poliisi Joshua Swisher pelasti kuljettajan savun täyttämästä Nissan Altimasta vain hetkeä ennen kuin ajoneuvo peittyi kokonaan liekkeihin. Kesäkuun 7. päivän tapahtumat tallentuivat sekä poliisiauton kojelautakameraan että Swisherin vartalokameraan, ja Southlaken poliisilaitos julkaisi videot myöhemmin. Tallenteissa näkyy, kuinka toisen liikennepysäytyksen yhteydessä alkanut tilanne muuttui nopeasti pelastustehtäväksi.

## Savuava auto ohjattiin tien sivuun

Swisher oli hoitamassa toista liikennepysäytystä Highway 114:n länteen johtavalla osuudella, kun hän sai radiolla ilmoituksen runsaasti savuavasta ajoneuvosta ja mahdollisesta autopalosta. Ilmoitus tuli lähes samanaikaisesti, kun hänellä oli jo toinen ajoneuvo pysäytettynä tien sivuun. Poliisiauton kameran mukaan savuava auto ohitti Swisherin, joten hän lähti sen perään. Hän kertoi ajatelleensa, että ajoneuvo oli saatava pysähtymään ja kuljettaja ulos ennen liekkien leviämistä.

Swisher sai kuljettajan ohjaamaan auton tien sivuun. Heti pysähtymisen jälkeen liekit voimistuivat, ja paksua mustaa savua alkoi virrata ikkunoista kuljettajan ollessa yhä sisällä. Vartalokameran tallenteella Swisher huutaa toistuvasti kuljettajaa poistumaan ja juoksee kuljettajan puoleiselle ovelle. Hän yritti avata oven ulkopuolelta, mutta kahva katkesi ja jäi hänen käteensä.

## Kuljettaja ulos rikotun ikkunan kautta

Oven avaamisen epäonnistuttua Swisher puki käsineet ja otti esiin ikkunan rikkomiseen tarkoitetun työkalun. Hän särki kuljettajan puoleisen ikkunan ja veti loukkuun jääneen miehen ulos autosta. Swisher kertoi, ettei nähnyt tiheän savun läpi auton sisälle. Hän erotti vain kuljettajan kädet tämän yrittäessä saada ovea auki sisäpuolelta. Ovenkahvan irrottua hänen oli ratkaistava nopeasti, miten kuljettaja saataisiin ulos.

Poliisin mukaan Nissan oli kokonaan liekkien peitossa vain sekunteja sen jälkeen, kun kuljettaja oli saatu turvaan. Kuljettaja ei loukkaantunut vakavasti. Swisher sai pelastuksen aikana vain lieviä palovammoja käsivarteensa. Hän kuvaili itse olleensa oikeassa paikassa oikeaan aikaan: savuava auto ohitti hänet samalla, kun hän hoiti toista liikennepysäytystä.

## Poliisilaitos palkitsi pelastajan

Southlaken poliisilaitos palkitsi Swisherin myöhemmin ansiokkaasta toiminnasta myönnettävällä tunnustuksella, joka on laitoksen toiseksi korkein kunnianosoitus. Poliisilaitoksen Facebookissa jakamat kojelauta- ja vartalokameratallenteet dokumentoivat tilanteen siitä hetkestä, kun savuava auto ohitti poliisin, siihen saakka, kun kuljettaja oli saatu ulos ja ajoneuvo peittyi liekkeihin.
summary_bullets: Joshua Swisher ohjasi voimakkaasti savuavan auton tien sivuun Southlakessa Texasissa.
Ovenkahvan irrottua poliisi rikkoi sivuikkunan ja veti kuljettajan ulos.
Kuljettaja välttyi vakavilta vammoilta, ja Swisher sai lieviä palovammoja käsivarteensa.
payload.journalist_note: Tapahtumien kulku on tarkistettu kahdesta uutisraportista. Päivämäärä, paikka, pelastustapa, vammat ja poliisilaitoksen myöntämä tunnustus vastaavat lähteissä kerrottuja tietoja.

Kuljettaja välttyi vakavilta vammoilta, ja Swisher sai lieviä palovammoja käsivarteensa.

article.source_text:
by ALEXX ALTMAN-DEVILBISS | The National News Desk SOUTHLAKE, Texas (TNND) — A Texas police officer is being recognized for a dramatic rescue after pulling a driver from a burning car just moments before the vehicle became engulfed in flames. Dashcam and body camera footage released by the Southlake Police Department shows Cpl. Joshua Swisher sprinting toward a smoke-filled Nissan Altima on June 7 while conducting an unrelated traffic stop along westbound Highway 114 in Southlake, Texas. Police said Swisher was alerted over his radio to a vehicle pouring heavy smoke as it approached his location. He directed the driver to pull onto the shoulder, but flames quickly intensified after the car came to a stop.

Body camera video shows Swisher repeatedly yelling, "Get out! Get out!" before rushing to the driver's door. When the exterior door handle snapped off in his hand, preventing him from opening it, he grabbed a window-breaking tool, shattered the driver's side window and pulled the trapped motorist to safety. Seconds later, the vehicle was fully engulfed in flames. "I could not even see inside the vehicle," Swisher told KDFW. "The only thing I saw was hands, and it was the driver trying to get his door open from the inside." The driver was not seriously injured, according to police. Swisher suffered only minor burns to his arm during the rescue. The Southlake Police Department later presented Swisher with its Meritorious Conduct Award, the department's second-highest honor.

The smoking vehicle had passed by Swisher on the highway, according to dashcam footage shared by the Southlake Police Department in a Facebook post. Swisher began following the vehicle in his car and had just directed it to the shoulder when it suddenly burst into flames. The dashcam and Swisher's body camera both captured the moment the burning car door handle broke off when he tried to open it. "Now, I'm thinking, 'How am I gonna get him out of this car?' And from there, I just put my gloves on," Swisher said. The camera footage shows thick, black smoke billowing from the car's windows with the driver still trapped inside. "I couldn't see inside the vehicle because of the amount of smoke that was pouring out," Swisher recalled.

Cpl. Joshua Swisher says he was at the "right place in the right time." A Texas police officer is speaking out after rescuing a driver from a burning car last month. Southlake Police Department Cpl. Joshua Swisher said he was responding to a traffic stop on June 7, along State Highway 114, when he received a call about a vehicle with heavy smoke pouring from it. "I had a vehicle pulled over on the shoulder, and almost simultaneously, dispatch alerted me to a smoke investigation, possible vehicle fire," Swisher told ABC News. "I was just thinking, 'I gotta get to that vehicle, get it stopped and pulled over, and see if I can't get that driver out of the vehicle before it goes up in flames.'"
